# railway_service_edge_rules (Resource)

Railway service edge rules. Replaces the whole set of edge rules of a service in an environment; destroying the resource clears them.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The rule format is defined by Railway; check it with the `validateServiceEdgeRules` API
# or the dashboard. The rule below is illustrative.
resource "railway_service_edge_rules" "example" {
  service_id     = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
  environment_id = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001"
  edge_rules = jsonencode([
    {
      expression = "http.request.uri.path eq \"/admin\""
      action     = "block"
    }
  ])
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `edge_rules` (String) JSON array of edge rules, usually built with `jsonencode`. Rules without an `id` get one assigned by Railway; fields Railway adds are not treated as changes.
- `environment_id` (String) Identifier of the environment the edge rules apply to.
- `service_id` (String) Identifier of the service the edge rules belong to.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Identifier of the edge rules, in the format `service_id:environment_id`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
#!/usr/bin/env sh

# Edge rules can be imported using `service_id:environment_id`.
# After import, `edge_rules` is read from Railway and shown as a diff against your configuration.
terraform import railway_service_edge_rules.example 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000:00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001
```
